source.product: No real product. An invented generic Japandi lounge armchair created for the hackathon demo catalogue; it does not depict or reproduce any manufacturer's design, and its price is invented demo data.
source.generation: Four-view turnaround reference sheet generated with the codex-image skill (front, three-quarter-front-left, side profile, rear on a seamless white studio backdrop), cut into four images with scripts/turnaround_crop.mjs, then Higgsfield generate_3d model multi_image_to_3d with all four views as role "image": should_texture=true, enable_pbr=true, should_remesh=true, topology=triangle, target_polycount=30000, symmetry_mode=auto, rigging and animation false, plus a texture_prompt describing oatmeal washed linen and pale oak legs.
source.postProcessing: npx @gltf-transform/cli resize --width 1024 --height 1024 (textures only, geometry untouched; 11.31 MB -> 3.30 MB), then scripts/fit_glb.py 82 85 78 to centre the footprint, put the base at y=0 and scale toward the listing size.

knownLimitations: Dimensions are a visual proxy, not a measured product. Against the intended 82 x 85 x 78 cm the asset measures 85.5 x 85.0 x 74.5 cm: 3.5 cm too wide and 3.5 cm too short, with depth exact. fit_glb.py hit its 10% anisotropy cap and exited 1, so this model would not pass the 2 cm / 3% tolerance in backend/api/test_furniture_assets.py without a budget entry.
Viewed from below the floor plane the underside of the seat is a flat dark untextured cap. It is not visible once the chair stands on the floor, which it does (measured minY = 0.0 cm).
The linen renders paler and cooler than the intended #e6e0d4 warm oatmeal, closer to a very pale greige.
Reconstructed from generated reference images, not from photographs of a real object; small-scale detail such as piping and seam placement is approximate.

No manual Blender inspection or correction pass has been done. Verified by rendering the GLB in model-viewer from front, rear three-quarter and low angles; geometry is clean and free of holes or floating fragments at those angles.
